data.name: Panjab
data.gender_notes: Panjab is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The land of five rivers - Beas, Sutlej, Ravi, Chenab, and Jhelum. The name Panjab carries the meaning “Five waters” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Punjab region in India tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Panjab usually hope their child will grow to embody five waters and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Panjab belongs to the Punjab region in India linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Five waters.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Panjab total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Panjab" holds a significant cultural impact as it represents the ancient region that lies in the north-western part of India, which is associated with the rich traditions and diverse cultures of its people. It is known as the land of five rivers - Beas, Sutlej, Ravi, Chenab, and Jhelum, providing fertile land and water for agriculture, which has been the backbone of the Punjabi economy and way of life for centuries. The name "Panjab" has also been historically linked to the valor and sacrifices of the brave heroes of Punjab, while their rich heritage is reflected through their vibrant arts, language, and cuisine, which continue to influence global cultures to this day.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Panjab holds great significance as it is believed to be the land where the sacred River Indus once flowed, which holds immense importance in Hinduism as the sacred waters of the Indus River are considered to be a symbol of the divine power of the universe. The sacred waters of the five rivers in Panjab are believed to be the embodiment of the divine presence of gods and goddesses, providing a constant spiritual connection between the people and their deities. This spiritual connection is reflected through the deep-rooted traditions and practices of the people, such as their devotion to their gods and goddesses, spiritual rituals, and meditation practices, which are an integral part of Punjabi life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Panjab: Land of Five Rivers. A symbol of unity and prosperity, where the five sacred rivers nourish the land and its people, fostering harmony and abundance.
